verdicts.flaw_description: In two of the four cases the height was measured before the fertilizer was applied within the stated season: the tomato was fed 3 August but measured 'by 20 June', and the oak was fed 2 May but measured 'by 19 April' (the other two, fed 8 January/measured 26 February and fed 7 October/measured 24 November, run forward). The effect therefore predates the treatment in half the cases.

The central syllabus 'doubled coursework's share of the final grade against the previous year' and 'every section was marked to that central syllabus', so all four sections were exposed to a grading change that by itself would raise coursework completion; it fits all four cases and is not separable from the lab kit.

The measured quantity is 'planned route time' (8, 5, 9 and 6 minutes below the earlier month), not actual delivery time; a routing change necessarily produces new planned times, so this shows the software's estimate fell, not that deliveries got faster.

The district 'attendance reward scheme ... tripled its payment that term' and 'every cohort was on the district roll that scheme covered', so all four cohorts got a large new financial incentive to attend during exactly the measurement window; that alone explains the 4-7 percent absence drop.
